item.title: TOEIC Day 11 Part3 アニメ業界のお金 — 店頭で交換のお願い
item.description: Excuse me, are you the clerk who handles exchanges? I bought this clothing item yesterday, but it's too small. Sure. Unfortunately, our policy cites a receipt for every exchange. Do you have one? I left it at home, but I paid by card. Can I still claim an exchange? Let me look closely at the tag. Is this the jacket made with the anime's choreographer? Yes. The studio wanted to collaborate with her, since goods earn more than the broadcast. That's a good point. I can combine your card record with the tag number. I'll go ahead and check the system.

item.title: TOEIC Day 10 Part2 ゲーム会社の決算 — 決算会議とお祝いの返事
item.description: Who will chair tomorrow's earnings meeting? Our CEO asked to lead it this time. Why don't we celebrate the strong results on Friday? Let's wait until the final figures are confirmed. Is the cast for the new game trailer confirmed yet? Ms. Lopez is in charge of that. Should we raise the price of the deluxe edition? It's a challenge. Costs may change, so use caution.

item.title: TOEIC Day 9 Part4 簿記・会計 — 電卓とレシートの店内放送
item.description: Attention, shoppers. Welcome to the Hillside Campus Bookstore. For a limited time, our new accounting calculators are available in aisle five. Each model has the capability to calculate taxes with just one button. Our bookkeeping software can also capture receipts from your phone. A local car rental agency and a wood carving studio already use it to track daily sales. Ask any clerk for a free demonstration. Please leave your old receipts in the blue bucket by the exit, and we will recycle them. The store will close in fifteen minutes. Thank you for shopping with us.

item.title: TOEIC Day 8 Part3 ブラッドボーン — プリンター故障とファンイベント
item.description: Hi, Daniel. The printer at the box office isn't working, and the Bloodborne fan event opens soon. I was wondering if it was the brand-new one we bought last week. Yes. It looks like the paper tray is stuck, so we can't print tickets. Why don't you check the old printer behind the bookcase? I'll call a technician. Good idea. Also, the botanist who arranged the flowers wants to meet during her break. That works for me. Her breathtaking garden display will appear in tonight's broadcast. I'll go ahead and bring the old printer. The spare tickets are in my briefcase.

item.title: TOEIC Day 7 Part2 エルデンリング — 攻略本の予約とイベント準備
item.description: 1. Did you reserve the Elden Ring guide book for me? I'll do it before the store opens tomorrow. 2. Whose binoculars are on the tournament table? They belong to the event staff, I think. 3. Aren't you studying biology at night school? Only on weekdays; weekend shifts here are a real benefit. 4. Where should I put the Elden Ring bedding display? Ms. Tanaka is drawing the layout on the board.

item.title: TOEIC Day 6 Part4 ダークソウル — ファンナイトの案内放送
item.description: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to our Dark Souls fan night. Our shop is headquartered in Osaka, and we are glad to see so many avid players in this banquet hall. Seats for the tournament are given on a first come, first served basis, so please find a table soon. Whether your background is in design, sales, or automotive work, everyone is welcome to join. Free baked goods are available at the back of the room. At nine o'clock, we will present an award to the winner of tonight's contest. Thank you, and enjoy the evening.

item.title: TOEIC Day 5 Part3 日本の時事 — 観光フェアの承認書と服装
item.description: Hi, Ken. I need your assistance with the travel report for the Osaka tourism fair. Sure. Did the auditor approve the budget yet? Not yet. She needs an authorization form first. Only authorized staff can sign it. I see. I will attach the receipts to the form and send it today. Thank you. Also, please assure the sponsors that the fair will go ahead. Of course. Should our team wear athletic shirts at the booth? No, business attire is better. We want visitors to take us seriously. Understood. I will email everyone this afternoon and bring spare name tags.

item.title: TOEIC Day 4 Part2 FCバルセロナ — ファンイベントの手配
item.description: Who will arrange the shuttle buses? Ms. Lopez on the events team. Yes, I rode one yesterday. At the main station. 2. Is the poster design finished? Yes, the manager approved it this morning, as planned. A print shop nearby. I designed my shirt. 3. When will the arborist visit the fan plaza? As soon as the rain stops. On the north side. I visited a zoo. 4. Would you like the architecture tour or the artisan market? The market, please. I appreciate the offer. Yes, I like it. It ends at five.

item.title: TOEIC Day 4 Part2 FCバルセロナ — 観戦イベントとクラブ会報
item.description: How many fans will come to the viewing event? Approximately two hundred, we think. The big screen is brand new. Yes, I enjoy football with my friends. Could you check this article for the club newsletter? Sure, as long as I can have it by noon. The newsletter arrives every month. My cousin is an archeologist. Who painted the artwork on the new scarf? A local designer did. Yes, the scarf is very warm. I will start the assembly of the shelves today. Where are the old match photos kept? They are in the club archive. Our young players are a great asset. Yes, they were taken last season.

item.title: TOEIC Day 4 Part2 FCバルセロナ — ファンクラブの総会と資料室
item.description: How long will the members' assembly last? Approximately two hours. It's in the main hall. Yes, I joined last year. Where can I find last season's match article? Try the club archive downstairs. It was a great match. Yes, I wrote it Monday. Can we hang this artwork in the fan museum? Sure, as long as the archeologist approves. The museum opens at nine. The painting took a month. The fan app is a real asset to the club, isn't it? Definitely, members use it every day. I forgot my phone charger. No, the club store is closed.

item.title: TOEIC Day 4 Part2 FCバルセロナ — ファンショップと資料室
item.description: How long will the assembly of the new display take? Approximately two hours. It will go in the fan shop. Yes, I assembled one last week. 2. Who is leading the talk about the old stadium site? An archeologist from the city museum. Next to the ticket office. Yes, it was a long talk. 3. Can I borrow some photos from the club archive? Sure, as long as you return them by Friday. The photographer left early. At the archive office. 4. The article calls our fan shop a big asset. Yes, many visitors come to see the artwork. I'll write the article tomorrow. The ticket office is closed today.

item.title: TOEIC Day 3 Part4 アニメ業界のお金 — 制作費の分析と追加資金の申請
item.description: Good morning, everyone. This is a quick update for the finance team at our animation studio. Our new series has an ambitious budget, so we must analyze every cost carefully. Apparently, the toy makers want to expand their orders, and we anticipate strong sales of goods. Please submit your application for extra funds by Friday. Also, the new approach to billing will improve the appearance of our monthly reports. We will discuss the details at ten tomorrow in Room B. Please bring your latest cost sheets. If you see any problem, send an alert to me right away. Thank you.

item.title: TOEIC Day 2 Part3 ゲーム会社の決算 — 広告費と管理費の会話
item.description: Hi, Ken. Could you turn on the air purifier before we review the quarterly earnings? Sure. The sales results look adequate, but our advertising costs were higher than planned. Why was that? We had to advertise the new game in three countries before the launch. I see. Did administrative expenses go up too? Yes, because an agency handled the hiring of extra staff. Then I advise you to add a note about it. The board will ask questions after the meeting. Good idea. I'll send you the draft in advance.

item.title: TOEIC Day 1 Part2 簿記・会計 — 監査・口座・売上目標・予算報告書
item.description: Who is going to accompany the auditor tomorrow? The accounting department manager will. He works for an acclaimed audit firm. Around nine in the morning. Have we opened an account at the new bank yet? Not yet. I need a bit of time to check. Yes, the bank closes at five. Please count the cash again. How can we achieve our sales target this quarter? By visiting a number of new clients. Yes, the target was too high. The quarter ends in December. Why is the budget report so short? Above all, the managers wanted a simple one. Yes, it is on the shelf. The printer is upstairs.

item.title: Day 76 ゲーム会社の決算 — 任天堂、Switch2販売減でも増益の理由
item.description: Nintendo's new console sold far fewer units this year, but profit still jumped sharply. On August 6, Nintendo announced its newest financial results for April to June 2026. Switch 2 sales fell 34 percent to 3.82 million units. Last year's launch had set an unusually high base. Even so, operating profit was lifted by strong software sales and a US tariff refund. The profit reached 142.6 billion yen, about two and a half times last year's figure. A hit movie, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, also boosted income after opening worldwide on April 1. It earned over one billion dollars, making it the second highest earning video game movie ever.

item.title: Day 74 日本の時事 — 高市内閣、急速な支持率低下
item.description: Sanae Takaichi became Japan's prime minister in October 2025, and her cabinet's approval rating was one of the highest in history. It reached 63.8 percent in November 2025, but by August 2026, support had fallen to just 48.4 percent. That must sound like a huge change for less than one year. Few new Japanese leaders have ever lost support so quickly. Many voters worry that cutting taxes could hurt funding for social security. In one survey, more than 75 percent said the government's explanation was not clear enough. Some analysts think her honeymoon period may already be over.

item.title: Day 72 アニメ業界のお金 — 市場最高でも人手不足で減収危機
item.description: Japan's anime production market has grown for five straight years. In fiscal 2025, companies earned about 406 billion yen, a new record, up 9.9 percent from last year. It was the first time sales had ever passed 400 billion yen. Although the industry looks richer than ever, many studios are struggling. They cannot find enough skilled animators to finish projects on time. As a result, 41 percent of specialist studios reported losses last year. That rate is far higher than it was the year before. Because of this shortage, experts warn 2026 could bring the first sales drop in five years.

item.title: Day 70 簿記・会計 — 監査人が不正を見つけるのはわずか6.6%
item.description: A report released by a Japanese startup studied seventy-six accounting fraud cases worldwide. You might expect auditors to catch fraud first, but they actually found only 6.6 percent of the cases. The most common cause was instead a sudden financial crisis inside the company itself. This single reason explained nearly 23.7 percent of all the cases studied. Many fraud cases were revealed by journalists, short sellers, and government investigators instead. Only 18.4 percent of all cases were caught by a company's own internal checks. The report therefore gives companies a clear and urgent warning about trusting auditors too much.

item.title: Day 68 FCバルセロナ — 収益10億ユーロ突破と支出上限アップ
item.description: FC Barcelona earned more than one billion euros last season, a new club record. Although Camp Nou was still being rebuilt, the team's income kept growing fast. The club played many home games at two smaller stadiums instead. Sponsorship deals and merchandise sales, which both hit record highs, pushed revenue even higher. In September, Camp Nou partially reopened with room for about 42,000 fans. This reopening let Barcelona's spending limit jump from 432 million euros to 583 million. Barcelona now has a larger amount of money to spend, but Real Madrid's limit is still higher.

item.title: Day 66 ゲーム会社の決算 — カプコン決算、驚きの高利益率
item.description: Capcom, the Japanese company behind the game series Monster Hunter, just reported surprising quarterly results. From April to June, its sales rose by 55 percent, reaching 70.4 billion yen, about 430 million dollars. Operating profit grew even faster, climbing 67 percent to 41 billion yen, which is almost 60 percent of total sales. This profit margin is higher than many famous technology companies achieve, although Capcom only makes games. Net profit also climbed sharply, rising 69 percent to 29.1 billion yen for the three-month period. Monster Hunter: World alone has already sold over 30 million copies worldwide, and Capcom hopes this growth continues.

item.title: Day 62 アニメ業界のお金 — 収益は伸びても赤字のカドカワ
item.description: Kadokawa, the Japanese company behind hit anime like Re:Zero, announced its latest earnings in August 2026. Revenue from its anime business, which covers April to June, grew by 27.4 percent year on year. Even so, the division posted an operating loss of 660 million yen, about four million dollars. Production costs had risen even faster than sales. Kadokawa said the costs of making anime, such as paying animators and studios, kept climbing during the quarter. To cut expenses, the company had already asked some staff to take early retirement earlier this year. From next quarter, it expects to save roughly 200 million yen from that earlier move.

item.title: Day 62 アニメ業界のお金 — 売上は過去最高なのに儲からない「利益なき好況」
item.description: The anime market in Japan reached a record 3.84 trillion yen in 2024. For the first time, overseas sales were larger than sales at home. This sounds like a happy story, which is only half true. IG Port, whose studios include Production I.G, saw animation sales rise 10.7 percent but still lost money. Rising costs for staff, CG, and outsourcing explain what is called a profitless boom. A research firm warns that the production market, which passed 400 billion yen in 2025, may shrink this year. So what matters is not the size of the market but where the money goes.

item.title: Day 60 簿記・会計 — 新リース会計基準でオフィス賃貸もB/Sに
item.description: Starting in April 2027, Japan will adopt a new accounting rule for leases. Until now, companies that rented offices listed the rent only as an expense. The old lease, which never appeared on the balance sheet, suddenly becomes visible. Under the new rule, almost every lease must be recorded as an asset and a liability. This is surprising because many managers thought renting was simpler than buying. Leases worth three million yen or less are still exempt. So are leases that last twelve months or less. The change follows international rules set in 2016. Experts say some companies' balance sheets will grow sharply, and their equity ratios may fall.

item.title: Day 54 日本の時事 — 日経平均、初の6万円超えの裏側
item.description: On April 23, 2026, Japan's Nikkei Stock Average closed above 60,000 yen for the first time. The index finished at exactly 60,013 yen, a surprisingly round number. The Nikkei tracks about 225 major Japanese companies, so this record affects many workers' pensions. Investors had wondered how long the rally could continue before this happened. Some experts say that higher stock prices do not always mean higher wages for ordinary people. In fact, real wages had been falling for months before the record was set. This gap between rising markets and shrinking paychecks surprised many citizens, who had expected better news.

item.title: Day 52 アニメ業界のお金 — 鬼滅の刃 無限城編、興収の内訳
item.description: Demon Slayer: Infinite Castle is a popular anime movie made by the studio Ufotable. It earned about 40.2 billion yen in Japan, becoming only the second Japanese film to pass that mark. Surprisingly, its worldwide earnings reached around 117.9 billion yen, almost three times the domestic total. The film stayed in Japanese theaters for 266 days, finally closing this April. That is close to nine months, which is unusually long for a movie here. Although the domestic numbers were already huge, fans around the world pushed the total even higher. This shows that anime has truly become a global business now.

item.title: Day 52 アニメ業界のお金 — ナルトは終了後も最高収益アニメに
item.description: Naruto is one of the most famous Japanese anime series. Its TV series actually ended back in 2017. However, Naruto has just become TV Tokyo's highest-earning anime franchise. TV Tokyo's anime rights business earned 27.22 billion yen last year, a rise of 17.8 percent. Most of this money was generated by overseas games and merchandise, not new episodes. China bought 31.1 percent of these rights, more than any other region. TV Tokyo's whole anime segment grew its profit by 55 percent this year. Clearly, a finished anime can still be more valuable than new ones.

item.title: Day 48 FCバルセロナ — カンプ・ノウ復帰と966億円の改修費
item.description: FC Barcelona finally returned to Camp Nou this year. The stadium had been closed for renovation since 2023. The project cost about 966 million dollars in total. When it finally reopens, Camp Nou will hold 99,354 fans. That makes it the largest stadium in Europe. Surprisingly, the club did not simply borrow this huge amount of money. Instead, president Joan Laporta sold future income, including media rights and shares in Barca Studios. Tickets for the comeback match sold out within hours. Many fans had been waiting more than two years to watch a game there. This return shows how much the stadium matters to the club.

item.title: Day 46 ゲーム会社の決算 — 任天堂、減収でも営業利益2.5倍
item.description: Nintendo's sales fell 9.5 percent from April to June, but operating profit was far higher than that of last year. Switch 2 hardware sales dropped 34.4 percent to 3.82 million units, yet software sales grew well. Even so, net profit still rose, reaching 96 billion yen. One reason was a tariff refund worth about 300 million dollars, and another was strong growth in Nintendo's IP business. This IP business, which includes movies and merchandise, grew 107.4 percent this quarter. These high-margin sales are more profitable than hardware sales. So profit grew even though total sales fell this quarter. Nintendo kept its full-year forecast unchanged despite this.

item.title: Day 44 日本の時事 — 最低賃金1177円、56円引き上げ
item.description: Japan's minimum wage will rise to 1,177 yen an hour from this October, a jump of 56 yen. That is the second-largest increase since the wage target system started back in 1978. In Kanagawa, where many care workers like nursing aides are employed, the new rate will be 1,279 yen. Some economists say this rise is being driven by Japan's shrinking workforce. As the labor force shrinks, companies must pay more to attract and keep staff. Even so, real wages have barely kept up with Japan's rising prices in recent years. For many part-time workers, this hourly pay is still not enough to live on comfortably.

item.title: Day 42 アニメ業界のお金 — 海外市場56.5%でも制作会社は25.5%しか受け取らない
item.description: Japan's anime industry earned 3.84 trillion yen in 2024, up 14.8 percent from the previous year. Growing fast overseas, the industry now earns 56.5 percent of its revenue from foreign markets. However, animation studios themselves receive only 25.5 percent of that overseas money. Toei Animation, known for producing Dragon Ball and One Piece, shows this gap clearly. Its production business earns a 28.1 percent profit margin, while its licensing business earns 54.6 percent. Struggling harder, IG Port actually lost money on production last year. A 2025 survey found that 60 percent of anime studios reported worsening results.

item.title: Day 40 簿記・会計 — 粉飾決算が急増、監査の目が厳しく
item.description: Twenty-seven listed companies in Japan admitted to committing accounting fraud in the first half of 2026. That total was actually a bit lower than the number recorded a year earlier. However, deliberate fraud, which experts call funshoku, almost tripled from the previous year. Stricter audits may explain why more of this hidden fraud is now being found. Manufacturing and information technology were the two industries with the most reported cases. In the technology sector, six of the seven cases involved fraud rather than honest mistakes. This pattern suggests that tougher checks are working, even though total numbers look calmer.

item.title: Day 38 FCバルセロナ — スタジアム改修に追加融資5.1億ユーロ
item.description: FC Barcelona members just approved a huge new loan. They need extra money to finish their stadium project. The full renovation was originally planned for this year. However, the work will not be completed until the 2028-29 season. Club leaders blame the war in Ukraine for part of the delay. Rising costs around the world also slowed the project down. In total, members approved 510 million euros in new financing. Of that, 300 million euros is a bond backed by stadium income. The remaining 210 million euros is guaranteed by future television revenue. Fans must now wait almost three more years to see the finished stadium.

item.title: Day 36 ゲーム会社の決算 — ソニー、ハード減でも最高益
item.description: Sony's PlayStation division earned a record operating profit for the year that ended in March 2026. Profit rose 11.6 percent to 463.2 billion yen, even though hardware sales were falling. PS5 hardware sales fell 2.5 million to 16 million units for the year, while digital sales and network services both grew strongly. Sony also wrote down 88.6 billion yen at Bungie, a studio it owns. If Sony had not taken that loss, its profit would have jumped by 45 percent instead. Total PS5 shipments have now passed 80 million units since 2020. Hardware is fading, but Sony's game business keeps setting new profit records.

item.title: Day 34 日本の時事 — 神奈川の最低賃金1,279円へ
item.description: Japan's minimum wage will rise across the whole country again this October. The national average will reach 1,177 yen per hour, which is 56 yen more than last year. Tokyo will keep the highest rate in Japan, at 1,280 yen per hour, as always. Surprisingly, Kanagawa's minimum wage will be raised to 1,279 yen, only one yen behind Tokyo's. This wage is decided by each prefecture every year, based on local living costs. Many part-time workers, who depend on this wage, will be affected by the change. Still, this rise may help people who are struggling to make ends meet.

item.title: Day 32 アニメ業界のお金 — 制作費高騰でも儲からない業界構造
item.description: The global anime market was worth 30 billion dollars in 2024, and it could grow to almost 100 billion dollars by 2037. Streaming platforms are a major reason, because they now order many original anime series. As a result, a single episode that used to cost about 15 million yen can now cost up to 60 million yen. You might think animation studios must be getting richer because of this boom. Surprisingly, most studios still receive only a fixed fee, so their profit rarely increases even if the anime becomes a huge hit. This gap between global popularity and local pay remains a serious problem in the industry.

item.title: Day 30 簿記・会計 — ASBJが会計基準を同時改正
item.description: On June 2, 2026, Japan's Accounting Standards Board revised two major accounting rules on the same day. One rule covers financial instruments, and the other covers consolidated financial statements, which are closely related topics. This was not a coincidence, because how a company values its financial instruments can affect its whole group's reported profits. Companies that use Japanese accounting standards must apply these new rules starting soon. Some companies have already begun studying the changes carefully, since the rules are quite technical. Even experienced accountants sometimes find these rules surprisingly difficult to fully understand at first.

item.title: Day 30 簿記・会計 — 不適切会計、12年ぶりの低水準
item.description: In fiscal 2025, only 35 listed companies in Japan disclosed improper accounting. That number fell 47.7 percent from the year before. It was the lowest total in 12 years. Of these cases, seven involved actual fraud. In the past, large companies with foreign subsidiaries often caused these problems. This year, however, cases on the Growth market increased instead. The Growth market lists many small, newer companies. So accounting problems are now shifting toward younger firms. This trend surprised many auditors and investors. They had expected fraud to keep rising, not falling.
